newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican farmers need gov't funding help-Ag council.
newsitem.headline: Mexican farmers need gov't funding help-Ag council.

text.p: Mexican farmers need an additional $3.1-$3.4 billion in government aid to keep funding at real levels and absorb expected lower grain prices, the president of the National Farming Council (CNA) Miguel Castro Sanchez told reporters on Wednesday.
The council sent a letter to the Agriculture Ministry on Wednesday asking for a 41 to 45 percent increase in the budget assigned to farmer aid programmes, Castro said.
"Above all, aid is needed in areas where basic grains are farmed," he said. Anticipated lower grain prices will strap farmers and require additional government aid, Castro said.
However, if the government does not boost its agriculture aid funds, production is unlikely to decline because crucial funding is doled out according to output, he added.
"The income will give more possible access to new technology, although without it crops will not decline but will be of lower quality," Castro said.
Castro estimated fewer grains will be imported in 1997 than in the past year, in which high import prices and grain shortages led to a trade deficit of about $1.302 billion.
Higher stocks in the beginning of the year of key feeding and consumer grains, sorghum, corn and beans, should help ensure less dependence on foreign crops, Castro said.
Mexican farmers were struck a double blow in 1996 as more imports were needed and grain prices soared.
In 1997, Mexico should return to regular import levels seen in 1993 and 1994 of six to seven million tonnes of grains, he said.
